known.title: Exclude older plan reads and reviews from the build count

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A developer runs `forge next` in an upgraded repo while another repo on the same machine runs a plan read or review using Forge v1.2.9.
`machine.view()` includes runs from other releases (`src/forge/machine.py:412`), but v1.2.9 records these runs with `started_at` and no `free` field (`v1.2.9:src/forge/machine.py:95`). This predicate consequently counts the read or review as a build, so a machine with no builds can report `Builds running: 1 of 4`.
findings.title: Exclude older plan reads and reviews from the build count

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - `forge next` is run while a worker is building.
Both client-history cases use an isolated machine registry and start no worker before calculating `used`, so the expected running count is always zero. An implementation that always prints zero would pass the only test of the new line. Exercise a live build and check the nonzero count through `forge next`.
